label: anim-target

check.0.instructions: In `candidate`, is the <property> of <part> the same as in `reference`?
In `screenshot`, does <part> meet this requirement: <property>? The specification it belongs to is in `specification`.

`frames` are 1 frames of a screen recording, in order of time (`seconds` is the time of each). Looking at how the picture changes from one frame to the next, does <part> meet this requirement: <property>? The specification it belongs to is in `specification`.

complexity.level.instructions: The images in `reference_images` are references for something that is going to be built to match them (an interface, a 3D model, a scene, an animation). How complex is it to build it so that it matches them? Rate the work of reproducing what the images show, not how important or well known the subject is.
criteria: A single plain shape or flat graphic with almost nothing to it and no fine detail, such as a plain cube, a solid-colour logo or one basic button.
A few plain elements laid out simply, with little detail: a basic screen with a handful of standard controls, or an object made of a few primitive shapes.
A moderate number of distinct parts with some detail or styling: an ordinary app screen, a recognisable object of several components, or a small scene with a few materials.
Many distinct parts with fine detail, layered materials, lighting or effects: a dense interface, a detailed model, or a scene with several kinds of surfaces.

A very large amount of intricate detail: a whole city or environment, an organic or highly detailed model with many parts, a scene with many interacting effects, or a screen of many interacting elements.

where.screen.instructions: The region of `candidate` that differs from `reference`.

instructions.question: Both images are enlarged crops that show <part>, cut out of two images. Is the <property> of <part> the same in `candidate_crop` as in `reference_crop`?

scoring: An item with checks: each check holds (the part is the same as in the reference, or the frames meet the requirement) or does not. A check that holds is right when it is judged PASS, a check that does not hold when it is judged FAIL; UNSURE is neither right nor wrong. The item is `correct` when none of its checks is judged the wrong way round (`false-pass`: a part that differs judged PASS, which must not happen; `false-fail`: a part that is the same judged FAIL), `exact` when every check is right: an item all UNSURE is correct and not exact, so read `exact` and the figures, not `correct` alone. A complexity item: right when the level the group reads as is in gold.accept, exact when it is gold.level; whether the groups read in the order of their rank is in the figures (`complexity`). The verdicts are the mod's (PASS from 0.9, FAIL up to 0.2; against a reference a PASS is the crop's and a whole image only fails, ADR 0008); the raw probabilities are kept with each answer, and `thresholds` gives what other bars would have said. Controls are the items in which nothing differs.

about.variants: `mod`: as the mod asks with the run's decision model: against a reference, Jev gets the checks and the Box questions in the first request and the zoomed re-check on the crops after it, pplx the first request alone; a motion is its frames in one request against its spec; a group of references is the complexity reading. `whole`: the first request alone with every decision model, so that what the zoomed re-check adds can be read from the two.
about.images: The experiment's pictures (2026-10-15), copied into eval/datasets/visual-check/; sized and cut as the mod does (core/image-files.ts, core/zoom-review.ts, sips). A motion is its 12 frames as files (8 of them for pplx), not a recording: the mod's ffmpeg is not run.

state.specification: A card slides in from the left over 12 frames, one every 50 ms (t=0 to t=550 ms). The end point is marked in every frame by a box the same size as the card, outlined in green dashes and labelled TARGET above it; the box is drawn on top of the card. The card should come to rest exactly inside the TARGET box.

checks.property: it never moves past the green dashed TARGET box and comes back (its right edge never goes beyond the right edge of the box and then returns: no overshoot, no bounce)
checks.why: the decision model is not sure either way

checks.property: it keeps moving until it reaches the TARGET box: it does not stay at the same position for several frames in the middle of the motion and then jump ahead

checks.part: the card in the last frame
checks.property: it sits exactly inside the green dashed TARGET box
